newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bull run steals show in Central Europe.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bull run steals show in Central Europe.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange outperformed other markets in the region this week, scoring records as foreign funds poured money into the market.

Similar reasons bolstered a more modest price rise in Warsaw, while Bratislava's gains seemed vulnerable. Prices firmed in Bucharest too, but Prague paid the price of last week's rally. Ljubljana ended a shade weaker.
The Central European Share Index (CESI) which measures the price movements of 73 Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Slovenian and Slovak stocks, firmed 2.5 percent during the week.
BUDAPEST
Hungarian share prices surged this week to surpass previous highs in the bourse's six-and-half-year history.
On Thursday, the BUX index closed at a fourth successive record high of 5,126.39 points, up 411.89 points or 8.74 percent over the week.
"Economic circumstances are favourable, results are growing, companies are good and the region is attractive," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities.
"Fund managers have to spend their money and when buying stocks they are opening positions worth at least half a million to a million dollars."
WARSAW

Polish shares, having broken a 33-month high earlier in January, set its sixth record this month on Thursday after Wednesday's dip. Analysts said the bull run, fuelled by apparent foreign buying, should continue but at a slower pace.
"Yesterday we had a correction and now it seems we'll have stability or more growth," said Bogdan Kornacki, a trader at Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) brokerage on Thursday.
Analysts said foreign institutions were still buying perhaps because regional bourses seemed a better deal compared to some foreign exchanges.
The main market's all-share WIG index closed at 15,846.7 points on Thursday, up 427.8 points or 2.8 percent from last Friday's close. The WIG rose 6.8 percent last week.
PRAGUE
The Czech PX50 index dropped back this week after a string of sharp gains in the first week of trading this year.
Blue chips took the brunt of the losses, especially the new year's star performer, power utility CEZ, which rose to a peak of 1,070 on Monday but fell back in the next two sessions.

"Most people realised some profit and they see the price (of CEZ) a little bit high...so maybe they are starting to be worried that the price has reached a peak," said Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostneska Banka in Prague.

In the broader market, brewer Pivovar Radegast posted some strong gains following an announcement by Britain's Bass Plc last week that it had increased its stake in the firm to 33 percent, and was mulling the possibility of eventually merging it with Prazske Pivovary in which it holds a majority stake.
BRATISLAVA
The Bratislava Stock Exchange saw a week of moderate, gradually growing activity, but brokers warned the growth was fragile due to a constant lack of liquidity.
The 12-share SAX index gained 5.36 points from the rising blue chips' prices and closed at 184.83 points on Thursday.
Traders said the market had been expected to decline in the near future, with investors apparently waiting for a drop in the value of the most demanded issues.
"Investors, playing on our market are also aware of the fact that there is still only few of them here," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
ZAGREB
Almost all Croatian stocks scored new gains this week in expectatio of the good sovereign credit rating that emerged on Friday.
Traders said they expected stocks to stablise or move higher next week.
"Croatia is finally on the map of foreign buyers," said Nenad Pavletic of Auctor brokerage.

Blue chip drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka continued to forge ahead, breaking records day after day. They closed at 540 and 1,700 kuna respectively on Thursday after their GDRs peaked at all-time highs in London on Wednesday.
LJUBLJANA

Slovenian shares eased one percent this week bringing the 10-share SBI-index down 12.7 points to 1,277.8 points. Financial consultancy Nika underperformed the market, plunging 7.9 percent, while construction firm GPG was the top gainer adding 9.2 percent to its price.
BUCHAREST
Strong buying interest powered stock prices upwards on the Bucharest bourse this week with traders expecting the bullish mood to continue in the first session next week.
Brokers said buoyant sentiment was prompted by a depreciation in the local currency, the leu, which has shed some 20 percent to 4,950/5,050 to the dollar since January 1.
The two unofficial indices, Vanguard SA 's VAB and Bucharest Investment Group 's BIG, rose by five percent and 4.97 percent, respectively, from the previous session.
